clue.text: To cover piano, trace woven rug

indicators.note: the shuffled letters cover, or sit around, the single letter for piano
woven means twisted together, so the letters of trace are rearranged

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Instructions for draping something over a piano, or a weaver tracing a design into a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' turns TRACE into CARET; 'To cover' puts that around P. 'To cover' reads like the definition (the verb sense fits too), but the definition is 'rug'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug is a floor covering, and a carpet is the larger version of the same thing.

parts.note: a rose is used for a lovely woman, as in an English rose

explanation.surface: A lovely woman made her entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of the verb meaning came up or came into view, matching the past-tense clue word.

clue.text: Image surprisingly cool for an orchestral instrument

parts.note: pic is a short informal word for a picture or image

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of cool turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A picture strangely cool enough to stand in for something in an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' gives COLO; 'Image' is the informal word for a photo, not a general picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The small high-pitched flute played in orchestras and military bands is an example of an orchestral instrument.

indicators.note: almost finished means the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tank is a large container like a vat

explanation.surface: A brown vat that is nearly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' drops the final K from TANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour word: a yellowish-brown shade, as of skin after sun exposure or tanned leather.

clue.text: Name occupying chair with English governing body

indicators.note: occupying means sitting in, so the name letter goes inside the word for chair

parts.note: a seat is a chair

explanation.surface: A name in the chair of an English governing body, as at a committee meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts N inside SEAT, giving SENAT, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative assembly, such as the upper house of a parliament, is a governing body.

clue.text: In giving off vapour, water finally flowing

indicators.note: In tells us the final letter goes into the word for giving off vapour

parts.note: steaming means emitting steam or vapour

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of water

explanation.surface: Steam rising off water that is running along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from water; 'In' puts it inside STEAMING. 'giving off vapour' looks like the definition, but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Running in a continuous stream, as water pours, is a synonym for flowing.

definitions.meaning: music is written down in notes, so it is set down in notation

explanation.surface: Music described as famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: renowned, and written in musical notes as a score is.

indicators.note: when drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk hitting the bar counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat someone heavily is a stronger synonym for beat in a contest.

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the party whose members are called Tories
a cent is a coin, a small sum of money
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A Conservative's spending allowance draws public notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Focused mental effort on something is a synonym for attention.

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Admiration for a bronze sculpture by Rodin, the French artist who made The Kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring 'love' means nothing; the romantic sense fits Rodin's sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a score of nothing is called love, so it is a sporting synonym for nought.

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for coming together surrounds the right letter

parts.note: banding together means uniting or coming together

explanation.surface: People uniting around the right to label things.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking or naming something with a brand or a stigmatising tag is a synonym for labelling.

parts.note: hopeless means very poor at something, bad
Thomas Minton founded the Minton pottery firm in Stoke-on-Trent

explanation.surface: An inept potter playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Minton is a famous English pottery maker; 'potter' looks like idling about.
explanation.definitionFit: The racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net is an example of a game.

definitions.meaning: what comes after first in order is the next ordinal
a brief unit of time, one sixtieth of a minute

explanation.surface: Something wins at the very first attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal after first, and a short unit of time measured by clocks.

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of monologue
inadequately suggests the letters of learnt are put together badly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: An actor's never-ending speech, poorly memorised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E; 'inadequately' rearranges LEARNT into TERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for ever, without end, is a direct synonym for everlasting.

clue.text: Country is requiring return of king

indicators.note: return of means the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's tragedy King Lear

explanation.surface: A nation needing its monarch back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' gives RAEL; the king is Shakespeare's, not a real monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation on the Mediterranean, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Again begin to relax with painting

parts.note: to rest is to relax
painting is an example of art

explanation.surface: Taking up a hobby again: unwinding with a paintbrush.
explanation.definitionFit: To start over is a synonym for beginning again, as with a computer or a race.

parts.note: to see is to observe
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: Look at this item: absolutely livid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a, an or the, but here it is an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling with anger, as liquid bubbles, is a figurative synonym for being furious.

clue.text: Skimpy underwear awfully hot, no good

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of hot are badly disordered

parts.note: N is short for no, as on a yes/no form

explanation.surface: Revealing underwear: terribly hot, but no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimal undergarment with a narrow strip at the back is an example of skimpy underwear.

indicators.note: backfiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wrestling in the bedroom tends to go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese sport of heavyweight grapplers pushing each other out of a ring is a form of wrestling.

indicators.note: in means the left letter is placed inside the word for pit

parts.note: a mine is a coal pit

explanation.surface: A children's writer abandoned in a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne, creator of Winnie-the-Pooh, is an example of a children's author.

indicators.note: moves suggests the letters of not nice shift into a different arrangement

parts.note: stable means steady, firm

explanation.surface: Someone sure that unpleasant manoeuvres are steadying.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond dispute, so sure and undeniable, is a synonym for certain.

clue.text: Form of transport coming up, one has a periscope

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle surfacing, with a periscope on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns BUS round in this down entry; it also fits a vessel surfacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine, the vessel that looks above water through a periscope, is described cryptically.

parts.note: a regiment's or ship's colours are its flag

explanation.surface: Colours painted on a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vessel for serving wine or ale, with a handle and spout, is a kind of bottle.

definitions.meaning: a type of English beer, well hopped and amber-coloured

explanation.surface: An acidic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in taste, and a British hoppy draught beer often served in pubs.
